title: Crown and Spire
premise: Quentin Eriksen, royal food-taster by day and ledger-keeper for the Gilded Spoon—a guild that trades in impossible things—has spent years making himself unnoticeable, dosing his own body against poison and his heart against attachment. When the border wards collapse the same night every star in the sky gutters out, he learns the court beneath the mountain has been harvesting starlight by buying souls, including the soul of Wren, the young apprentice he secretly considers family. To reclaim it, Quentin must trade the one thing he has hoarded all his life: his carefully cultivated invisibility, which turns out to be a rare and corruptible magic the under-court craves. In the end he sells his own name to buy Wren's soul back, extinguishes the last dragon-fire rather than let the under-court seize it, and—nameless but remembered by his found family—chooses to be seen at last.
about_author: Ulyana Nakamura is a former pastry chef who spent a decade working palace-adjacent kitchens before turning to fiction, a history that flavors her obsession with servants, secrets, and what royalty swallows without tasting. She writes from a drafty apartment above a tea shop, where she keeps ledgers of her own—mostly of debts owed to cats.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A routine morning tasting for the paranoid King Aldous, intercut with Quentin's nightly bookkeeping for the Gilded Spoon, where entries include bottled laughter and a winter sold on credit. We meet Wren, the apprentice who insists on calling him family. Emotional beat: cozy routine hiding deep loneliness.

chapters.title: Impossible Inventory
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A client tries to trade a memory of the sea for a second chance at a first love, and Quentin must price the unpriceable. Guild mistress Ovelia warns him that the under-court beneath the mountain has been an unusually hungry buyer lately. Emotional beat: unease beneath the guild's charm.

chapters.title: Wren Sings to the Dark
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, an orphan with a voice that makes candles lean, confesses she's been meeting a courteous stranger who pays her in starlight for small songs. Quentin, alarmed, forbids it—and Wren, hurt, accuses him of keeping everyone at arm's length. Emotional beat: first fracture in the found family.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Mid-feast, every star vanishes and the border wards fall with a sound like a snapped harp string. In the chaos, Wren disappears, leaving only a receipt in Quentin's own ledger hand: one soul, sold, to the Court Beneath. Emotional beat: terror and guilt.

chapters.title: Ash on the Ledger
chapters.summary: Ovelia's POV. The guild convenes in emergency session; impossible things are failing across the city—bottled storms going flat, sold luck souring. Ovelia reveals the under-court has been buying souls as fuel to drag the stars down. She forbids Quentin from going after Wren. Emotional beat: institutional fear versus personal loyalty.

chapters.title: What the King Cannot Taste
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin realizes the king's nightly tonic is laced with something that dulls the court's memory of the stars—and traces it to the royal alchemist, who is under-court's creature. Staying invisible is now complicity. He pockets the vial and decides to act. Emotional beat: the taster becomes the poison.

chapters.title: A Debt Owed in Dragon-Fire
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin seeks Brammel, the last dragon, guttering in a mountain cave like a dying lamp, whose fire once sealed the wards. Brammel agrees to relight them—for a price Quentin can't yet pay—and lets slip that Quentin's 'invisibility' is not caution but a rare magic: the gift of being unremembered. Emotional beat: awe and dread at his own nature.

chapters.title: The Gilded Spoon Turns Its Back
chapters.summary: Ovelia's POV. Ovelia expels Quentin for stealing guild secrets to bargain with the under-court, revealing the guild has an old, shameful treaty with it. Her hardness masks fear for him. Emotional beat: exile from the only structure he trusted, and the reader sees Ovelia's grief.

chapters.title: Down the Stair That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Using his unremembering gift, Quentin slips past the palace guard and finds the hidden stair beneath the mountain, guided by a map written in Wren's hand and smuggled out by a sympathetic kitchen maid. Emotional beat: descent, literal and moral; resolve hardening into recklessness.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The under-court is beautiful and wrong: nobles wearing borrowed faces, chandeliers of caged starlight, Wren's song echoing from a vault. Quentin strikes a bargain with the Under-King—he will trade his invisibility magic for Wren's soul, payment due in seven nights. Emotional beat: seduction and horror entwined.

chapters.title: Wren in a Glass Case
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, soul half-removed, exists as a fading echo in the vault, remembering Quentin in fragments. Her chapter reveals the under-court's hunger: they were once the stars' own keepers, exiled and starved. Emotional beat: pity for the enemy, and Wren's stubborn spark of self.

chapters.title: Seven Nights of Ordinary Things
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Back on the surface, Quentin spends his last week of selfhood doing deliberately unremarkable things—eating street noodles, mending Ovelia's ledgers anonymously—trying to feel what a life is worth. Emotional beat: tender, elegiac; power's price made intimate.

chapters.title: The Alchemist's Confession
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin confronts the royal alchemist, who confesses the court above sold its memory of the stars generations ago to buy peace—and that Quentin's parents were tasters who made the same bargain Quentin is about to. Emotional beat: generational doom; Quentin refuses the pattern.

chapters.title: Ovelia's Oldest Entry
chapters.summary: Ovelia's POV. Ovelia finds Quentin's anonymous repairs and the first ledger page she ever wrote: a debt the guild owes to Quentin's parents, unpaid. She breaks the guild's treaty, burning her copy, and sets out after him. Emotional beat: institutional corruption confronted by personal honor.

chapters.title: The Under-King's Offer
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The Under-King reveals the true price: not Quentin's gift, but Quentin himself—unremembered by everyone above, he would make a perfect, invisible warden of the vault. He shows Quentin how beloved he'd become, then how quickly he'd be forgotten. Emotional beat: the corruption of power offered gently.

chapters.title: Brammel's Last Ember
chapters.summary: Brammel's POV. The dragon, nearly out, reflects on every bargain he's witnessed and chooses to spend his final fire not on the wards but on forging one true thing: a key of flame that can open the soul-vault once. Emotional beat: sacrifice; the old world's last light spent on the new.

chapters.title: The Price of a Name
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. At the vault, Quentin signs away his name to free Wren—but Ovelia arrives with the ledger and invokes the guild's oldest law: a debt to Quentin's parents cancels the sale. The Under-King, enraged, moves to take all three of them. Emotional beat: found family arriving exactly when it matters.

chapters.title: Vault of Caged Light
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, then Wren's. Quentin uses Brammel's key to open the vault; freed starlight floods the dark, and Wren's soul returns to her mid-song. The under-court, starving, reaches for the light—and Quentin must choose between hoarding it for the escape and giving it away. Emotional beat: climax of generosity versus survival.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon-Fire
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Rather than let the Under-King seize Brammel's dying flame, Quentin feeds the last dragon-fire to the freed starlight, reigniting the stars themselves and collapsing the under-court's stolen splendor. The Under-King, diminished to a cold small thing, is left with only his hunger. Emotional beat: triumphant, costly, luminous.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: Ovelia's POV. Above ground, the city wakes to stars it doesn't remember losing. Ovelia reopens the guild under new law: nothing with a soul may be traded. She writes Quentin's name back into the ledger by hand, since no magic will do it. Emotional beat: quiet repair of institutions by stubborn people.

chapters.title: The Taster Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin returns to the king's table, but no longer invisible: the new alchemist, the maid, Ovelia, and Wren all know him. He tastes the king's soup and, for the first time, adds salt. Emotional beat: belonging chosen openly, power renounced gladly.

chapters.title: Crown and Spire
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A year on: Wren apprenticed to the guild, singing to relit stars; Brammel's cave a shrine tended by strangers; Quentin nameless in no record but remembered in every one that matters. On the spire above the palace, the family shares a meal. Emotional beat: found family as the only crown worth keeping.
